es.summary: El médico o la obstetra rompe la bolsa amniótica con un instrumento estéril (amniotomía). Se usa sobre todo para inducir o conducir el trabajo de parto.
key_points: Se hace con un gancho estéril que abre un pequeño orificio en la bolsa y deja salir el líquido lentamente.
La cabeza fetal debe estar encajada antes de la amniotomía para disminuir el riesgo de prolapso del cordón.
Junto con oxitocina, acelera el trabajo de parto alrededor de 1 a 1,5 horas.
Riesgos principales: infección (corioamnionitis) y prolapso del cordón umbilical.

usage: Ejemplo: «RAMO a las 10:00, líquido claro, FCF 140 lpm posterior».
Se anota en el partograma junto con la dilatación y la DU.
nursing_care: Verificar el consentimiento informado y explicar el procedimiento.
Valorar la FCF antes e inmediatamente después del procedimiento.
Observar color, olor y presencia de meconio en el líquido.
Registrar fecha, hora, quién lo realizó, características del líquido y valoración materno-fetal.

en.summary: The provider breaks the amniotic sac with a sterile instrument (amniotomy; RAMO in Spanish). It is used mainly to induce or augment labor.
key_points: The health-care provider uses a sterile amniotomy hook to puncture a small opening in the amniotic sac, causing the slow release of amniotic fluid.
The fetal head must be engaged in the pelvis prior to an amniotomy to reduce the risk of a prolapsed cord.
When amniotomy was performed for labor augmentation in combination with oxytocin administration, labor was shown to be expedited by 1 to 1.5 hours.
Main risks: infection (chorioamnionitis) and umbilical cord prolapse.

usage: Example: "AROM at 10:00, clear fluid, FHR 140 bpm afterward".
Recorded on the partograph along with dilation and contractions.
nursing_care: Confirm informed consent and explain the procedure.
The nurse monitors the fetal heart rate before and after the amniotomy.
Assess the amniotic fluid's color, odor, and the presence of meconium.
Document the date, time, provider's name, amniotic fluid characteristics, and maternal and fetal assessments.

sources.name: Maternal-Newborn Nursing: Nursing Care during the First Stage of Labor

summary.0.quote: The health-care provider uses a sterile amniotomy hook or instrument to puncture a small opening in the amniotic sac, causing the slow release of amniotic fluid.

key_points.0.quote: The health-care provider uses a sterile amniotomy hook or instrument to puncture a small opening in the amniotic sac, causing the slow release of amniotic fluid.

key_points.1.quote: The fetal head must be engaged in the pelvis prior to an amniotomy to reduce the risk of a prolapsed cord .

key_points.2.quote: When amniotomy was performed for labor augmentation in combination with oxytocin administration, labor was shown to be expedited by 1 to 1.5 hours.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: Informed Consent: The nurse witnesses that the procedure, as well as the reasons for the amniotomy, potential benefits, risks, and alternatives, has been explained to the patient.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: The nurse closely monitors the patient’s uterine contractions and fetal heart rate patterns before and after the amniotomy.

sections.nursing_care.2.quote: After the amniotomy, the nurse monitors the characteristics of the amniotic fluid, including color, odor, and the presence of meconium (fetal stool).

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Accurate and detailed documentation of the procedure, including the date, time, provider’s name, amniotic fluid characteristics, and maternal and fetal assessments, is essential in the patient’s medical record.
